items.title: Migrate a Postgres database to Lakebase (Beta)
items.text: You can now copy an existing PostgreSQL database into a Lakebase project in a single, one-time migration. Lakebase assesses the source database for compatibility, then copies its roles, schema, and data to a branch that you choose. Migrations are available in the Lakebase App and through the Postgres API and SDKs, with no separate enablement step. See Migrate a Postgres database to Lakebase for migration steps and region availability.

items.title: Lakewatch streaming detection rules (Experimental)
items.text: Lakewatch now supports streaming detection rules, which evaluate each new row of a source table as it arrives and create a signal for every row that matches a SQL predicate. Use them for low-latency signature, indicator of compromise (IOC), and atomic-signal detections. Lakewatch manages the compute, so you don't select a SQL warehouse or a schedule. Streaming rules are an experimental feature. See Streaming detection rules.

items.title: Genie Migrate conversion to Lakeflow pipelines is generally available
items.text: Genie Migrate conversion of T-SQL scripts from SQL Server and Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pools into Lakeflow pipelines is now generally available. In a T-SQL migration project, choose the Spark Declarative Pipelines target framework, organize your files into groups, and choose a catalog and schema for each group. Each group becomes one serverless pipeline that Genie Migrate validates with a dry run. To use the Spark Declarative Pipelines target framework, a workspace admin must turn on Migration Projects Experimental Features from the Previews page. See Manage Azure Databricks previews. See Supported source dialects and target frameworks.

items.title: Outbound IP addresses for serverless compute are generally available
items.text: Published outbound IP addresses for serverless compute are now generally available. Previously, they were in Public Preview. Azure Databricks publishes the outbound IP addresses in ip-ranges.json. To allow serverless compute through a firewall that protects your resources, add these IP addresses to its allowlist and automate updates as the IP addresses change. See Configure access to other resources using outbound IP addresses.

items.title: Nov 23, 2026: Support for multiple tag-based row access policies (Preview)
items.text: Support for applying multiple tag-based row access policies to the same table or view is now available in preview. By default, the policies are combined with AND. To combine them with OR, specify PERMISSIVE when you set the policy on the tag.

items.title: Nov 20, 2026: Container runtime for Streamlit apps in Snowflake Native Apps (General availability)
items.text: With this release, the container runtime for Streamlit apps in a Snowflake Native App is now generally available. Providers can run a Streamlit app inside a Snowflake Native App as a Snowpark Container Services service on a compute pool that the app creates and owns in the consumer account, instead of on a virtual warehouse.
